newsitem.title: UK: UK can afford above trend growth - CBI's Barker.
newsitem.headline: UK can afford above trend growth - CBI's Barker.

text.p: Britain can get away with a year of above trend growth without causing an unmanageable explosion in inflation, said Kate Barker CBI chief economic adviser and member of the Treasury's panel of advisers.
"There is scope to grow above trend for a year without causing problems for inflation," she told Reuter on Monday.

She said the question of interest rates was a difficult one at the moment given how hard it was to gauge the level of performance in the service sector although it did not seem to be growing excessively.
She added that manufacturing was potentially still quite weak and retail sales not that strong.
"In every sector competitive conditions are very tight. There is still a lot of cost cutting around."
Asked whether the UK could afford to wait and see before raising its 6.0 percent interest rates, she replied "yes."
"We're not finding general skill shortages, services are quite strong, distribution is not quite back to 1987 levels. We still have an output gap," she said.
Calls are growing for a rise in British interest rates as the economy booms and there are fears that the official gross domestic product series is understating the level of growth.
Trend growth is 2.0 to 2.5 percent. Official data say the economy grew by 2.7 percent in the fourth quarter compared with a year earlier.

Worries over the rate of growth hit gilts on Monday following newspaper reports of a Lehman Brothers study suggesting the economy has actually been growing at an annual rate of around 4.0 percent in the past few quarters.
UK interest rates are expected to remain on hold until after the May 1 election.
